thread:
kirti (customer): Hi — seeing frequent mid-stream disconnects from our iOS/Android apps when users switch between wifi and cellular. Large responses (~10-15k tokens) often arrive partially then stream drops. Happening several times today across multiple customers. trace_id=tx-7a9c1b

anya (support): Sorry you're hitting this, kirti. Can you share repro steps and whether you're using EventSource / native SSE or an SDK? Any client logs or server trace ids helps.

kirti (customer): Using our React Native client with EventSource (polyfill). Repro steps: 1) start streaming generation; 2) toggle wifi off -> cellular on; 3) observe partial content then connection closed. Logs show "EventSource closed unexpectedly" and we get a 0-length error in the UI. Example client console: 
```
EventSource error: EventSource connection closed (event: message)\nlastEventId: \nreceived 2 partial chunks ("data: {...}\n") then nothing\n```
Trace ids: tx-7a9c1b, tx-7a9d2f (attached).

ryan (mobile-eng): Thanks. Two quick things we've seen: (a) mobile OS will aggressively tear sockets on network change and sometimes the JS layer doesn't surface the exact close code; (b) some carrier/proxy/NAT devices will silently drop long-lived connections after an idle window or when network attachment changes. Are you seeing any TCP FIN/RST on the device?

kirti (customer): No FIN/RST visible in RN logs — just the EventSource error above. Server side we see the stream aborted around the same timestamps. Server log snippet: 
```
[2026-02-20T14:12:03Z] INFO stream-start trace=tx-7a9c1b client=mobile-app user=kirti
[2026-02-20T14:12:25Z] WARN connection-reset trace=tx-7a9c1b reason="connection reset by peer"
[2026-02-20T14:12:25Z] ERROR stream-abort trace=tx-7a9c1b bytes_sent=18321
```
That bytes_sent value corresponds to partial output.

dave (sre): Looks like server is getting an abrupt TCP close. Common root causes: middlebox idle timeout, mobile OS, or client-side library not handling network switch. Two mitigations to try: (1) SSE keepalive (send comment lines like `:\n` every 15s) to prevent idle drops; (2) implement client-side network-change listener to re-open EventSource immediately on connectivity change and resume with `last-event-id` or by starting a new request with the same prompt + offset.

anya (support): Can you try a quick repro with curl from a laptop simulating a change? Example: open SSE with curl then kill the connection and re-open. Also try `--no-buffer -N` to stream. Example command we use for repro: 
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=fast-13b" --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```
If you interrupt the network (e.g., `sudo ifconfig en0 down` / up) do you see the same behavior?

kirti (customer): I ran that curl test on macbook and after toggling wifi it reconnects fine if I immediately restart curl. But on mobile the app doesn't auto-reopen and user sees a partial response.

ryan (mobile-eng): That's consistent — mobile browsers and RN polyfills often don't auto-retry SSE. For production we recommend: 1) client keepalive ping (if using native SSE, OS will handle TCP keepalive; polyfills may not), 2) add a small reconnect/backoff strategy that checks networkState API and reconnects quickly, 3) optionally use our SDK's streaming helper which has reconnection logic.

kirti (customer): Is there anything Redwood can do server-side to reduce partial outputs for these network switches? Customer is seeing bad UX because partial text often ends mid-sentence.

lex (eng-runtime): Server-side options: we can (A) add more frequent heartbeat frames (server comment `:\n`) to keep NAT mappings alive — this is low-risk and helps many mobile carriers, (B) buffer a small trailing chunk and mark finalization only after we detect a graceful close — but that increases memory and latency, (C) implement resumable streaming with chunk cursors (bigger change). Short term we can push more aggressive keepalives and instrument to count reconnects per trace id.

dave (sre): Also checking our edge/ingress: some load balancers have idle timeout = 60s. If the client's network switch causes a NAT mapping to expire, the new path won't be associated with the same 5-tuple and the upstream will see a reset. Keepalives reduce that. We should also surface a helper in docs about recommended keepalive interval for mobile (<= 15s).

anya (support): Action plan: 1) kirti, try client reconnection logic ASAP (network listener + immediate reconnect) and report if UX improves; 2) we (eng-runtime) will enable a short-term edge keepalive change (send comment lines every 10s) for the next canary to see impact; 3) add telemetry to track partial-stream events and bytes_sent at abort. Ticket RINF-2351 opened. @lex can you schedule the canary?

lex (eng-runtime): I'm rolling a canary with increased keepalive to our edge pool now (small percent) — deploy-bot will post status.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: edge/keepalive=10s -> 5% of traffic. id=deploy-7781 status=started

kirti (customer): Thanks — I'll try the client fix today and report back. If you can link to the ticket I'll forward it to our PMs. :thumbsup:

dave (sre): One more debug tip — if you can capture the device's packet capture during the switch we can confirm whether there's an RST or just silent drop. If it's a silent drop, keepalives will likely fix it.

anya (support): Noting next steps and assigning RINF-2351 to eng-runtime + mobile-eng. Will follow up once canary metrics come back (reconnect rate, partial-stream rate). :rotating_light:

kirti (customer): Uploaded a short screen recording and device logs to the ticket. Thanks all.

lex (eng-runtime): Canary health looks okay so far (no obvious error spike). Will keep it at 5% for 2h then expand if stable.

deploy-bot: Canary update: deploy-7781 status=healthy 5% -> 5% (2m)

anya (support): Closing loop — please re-open thread or ticket if you still see mid-stream partials after client reconnect logic + canary expansion. Appreciate the detailed repro steps, kirti.
